independent.summary: After a refused switch (404), the select keeps showing the rejected workspace while the session still acts in the old one; the one-way `:value` binding is unchanged so Vue never re-patches the DOM value, and the `id === workspace.value?._id` guard plus an unchanged binding on re-open leave the control stuck displaying the wrong workspace.

grades.reason: The reload is the deliberate, documented design (the entity list, type registry and `/events` stream are all bound to the workspace being left) and is triggered only by an explicit user switch after the server has already committed the choice; no unsaved-state path is identified in this code.

`resolveWorkspace` re-checks the selected id against the caller's live membership list on every request (`server/src/middleware/workspace.js:192-206`) and falls back to the default, so a stale session id grants no access at all — the id is left in the session on purpose, documented against the `/events` long-response save race, and `resave: false` in `app.js:111` means no stale write-back occurs.
Same claim as finding 2 about the session id not being cleared, just anchored in the route file instead of the middleware — and equally untrue, since membership is re-verified per request.

`workspaceSelect.test.js` has a dedicated `describe('a selection whose membership is then removed')` that revokes the membership and asserts `GET /workspace`, `GET /entities` and a write all resolve the default workspace instead of 403.

triageGrades.reason: The change rewrites `resolveWorkspace` (the tenancy/authorization boundary) and adds a membership-checked selection route with its own 401/404 handling.
No credential, token or secret handling is added or altered; the test's `delete process.env.BEARER_TOKEN` is env hygiene, not secret management.
Nothing touches billing, allowances or AI cost accounting; per-workspace billing is explicitly out of scope.
No product-code deletes or data migrations; the only `$pull`/raw update is inside the test fixture setup.
All new calls are internal (Mongo plus the app's own REST routes); no outbound third-party request is introduced.
Only source, tests and docs changed — no deploy config, versioning, build or migration step.

summary: The local review found no real defects: two of its four findings restate the same mistaken claim that a stale session selection grants access (the middleware re-checks membership every request), one objects to a deliberate documented reload, and one asserts a missing test that the suite plainly contains — while the one genuine (if minor) UI-desync defect in the switcher went unnoticed; triage was entirely correct.
